questions: Are you here because of a new swelling or mass?
Is the swelling located in the lower abdomen, groin, or genital area?
Is the area red, warm, or draining fluid?
Do you have fever or chills?
Are you vomiting or unable to keep fluids down?
Are you unable to urinate or pass stool or gas?
Have you had vaginal bleeding or unusual discharge?
Have you recently had surgery, an injury, or childbirth?
Have you ever had a similar swelling before?
Do you feel faint, short of breath, or have chest pain?

DIAGNOSIS: Developmental dysplasia of the hip with unilateral congenital hip dislocation

Alternative 1: Proximal femoral focal deficiency (congenital femoral hypoplasia)

Alternative 2: Congenital limb-reduction defect due to amniotic band sequence

Alternative 3: Congenital unilateral femoral shortening from a skeletal dysplasia
